skill.name: security-audit
skill.description: Guide a read-only security audit of command execution, tool permissions, secrets handling, WebSocket access, and frontend risks.
skill.summary: Guides read-only security reviews for AI application deployment readiness.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged inline Markdown references to filenames, tool names, a route, and python-dotenv. Manual review found no executable code, no instruction to run commands, and no prompt injection attempt in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 10 is a Markdown checklist heading that names backend/main.py in inline code. It does not execute a shell command or instruct execution.
Line 11 asks the auditor to inspect run_terminal_command() for injection risk. This is documentation about review scope, not executable backtick or shell behavior.
Line 16 lists allowed tool names in inline code as part of a permission review. It does not invoke those tools or run external commands.
Line 21 tells the auditor to verify that .env is ignored by version control. The inline code is a filename reference, not shell execution.
Line 23 mentions python-dotenv as a library to verify during secrets review. It is not a command invocation or dynamic execution path.
Line 26 references the /ws endpoint in inline code for an authentication check. This is a route name in documentation, not shell execution.
Line 23 asks the auditor to verify safe environment variable handling. The skill does not read environment files or request secret values.
Line 21 recommends checking that .env is listed in .gitignore. This reduces secret exposure and does not require opening or exposing .env contents.

content.user_title: Audit AI App Security Before Release
content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss command execution, tool permission, and secret handling risks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused checklist for read-only audits.
actual_capabilities: Reviews command execution flows for shell injection and timeout gaps.
Checks tool permission boundaries for chat and agent modes.
Audits secrets handling, including .env hygiene and hardcoded API keys.
Reviews WebSocket authentication, message validation, and user input handling.
Checks frontend risks such as markdown XSS and sensitive client-side data.
Produces findings grouped by critical issues, warnings, and recommendations.
limitations: It is a checklist-style audit guide, not an automated vulnerability scanner.
It depends on the model having read access to the target application files.
It does not exploit vulnerabilities or modify files during the audit.
It focuses on the security areas named in SKILL.md, not full compliance review.

use_cases.title: Pre-Deploy Review
use_cases.description: Run a focused security pass before shipping an AI-enabled application to production.

use_cases.title: Command Execution Audit
use_cases.description: Check terminal command handling for injection risk, missing timeouts, and unsafe patterns.

use_cases.title: Secrets and Permissions Check
use_cases.description: Review environment variable handling and tool access rules before adding new agent features.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a read-only security audit of this project. Focus on command execution, tool permissions, secrets handling, WebSocket security, and frontend risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Command Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the command execution path for shell injection, unsafe arguments, missing timeout enforcement, and risky command patterns. Report evidence and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Agent Permissions
prompt_templates.scenario: Permission boundary review for AI features.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the chat and agent tool permissions. Identify overly broad access, bypass paths, and places where user input can reach privileged tools.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Security Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release security audit and organize results into critical issues, warnings, and recommendations. Include file references, impact, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Run a security audit before deployment.
output: Critical issues: No critical issues found in the reviewed areas.
Warnings: Command execution accepts user-provided text without a documented allowlist.
Recommendations: Add explicit validation, keep the timeout enforced, and document approved commands.

output_examples.input: Check the WebSocket endpoint for security issues.
output: Authentication: The endpoint should reject unauthenticated clients before accepting messages.
Validation: Message fields should be schema-checked before use.
Follow-up: Add tests for malformed messages and unauthorized connections.

output_examples.input: Review secrets handling in the project.
output: Findings: No hardcoded keys were found in the reviewed files.
Warning: Confirm that local environment files are ignored by version control.
Recommendation: Load secrets from environment variables and avoid printing them in logs.

best_practices: Run the audit before production deploys and after changes to tools, authentication, or command execution.
Provide access to the relevant backend, frontend, and configuration files for a complete review.
Treat reported critical issues as blockers until a human reviewer confirms the fix.
anti_patterns: Using the audit output as proof of compliance without human security review.
Asking the model to exploit discovered vulnerabilities during the review.
Running the checklist on partial code and assuming unreviewed components are safe.

faq.question: Does this skill change project files?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that the audit is read-only and requires approval before implementation work.

faq.question: Which security areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers command execution, tool permissions, secrets handling, WebSocket security, and frontend security checks.

faq.question: Can it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It provides a focused review checklist and cannot replace full testing, threat modeling, or expert review.

faq.question: Does it need access to environment files?
faq.answer: No. It should verify safe handling without exposing or logging secret values.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should the final audit include?
faq.answer: The final report should list critical issues, warnings, recommendations, evidence, and practical remediation steps.
